router_body:
name: plan
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 5
    steps:
      - name: full job set selected
        if: ${{ github.event_name != 'pull_request' || contains(github.event.pull_request.labels.*.name, 'full-matrix') || contains(github.event.pull_request.labels.*.name, 'ci') || contains(github.event.pull_request.labels.*.name, 'release-matrix') }}
        run: echo 'SELECTED std-reference build'
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
        if: ${{ github.event_name != 'pull_request' || contains(github.event.pull_request.labels.*.name, 'full-matrix') || contains(github.event.pull_request.labels.*.name, 'ci') || contains(github.event.pull_request.labels.*.name, 'release-matrix') }}
      - name: local gate wiring proof
        if: ${{ github.event_name != 'pull_request' || contains(github.event.pull_request.labels.*.name, 'full-matrix') || contains(github.event.pull_request.labels.*.name, 'ci') || contains(github.event.pull_request.labels.*.name, 'release-matrix') }}
        run: python3 -I ci/local-gate-test.py
      - name: local evidence gate
        if: ${{ !(github.event_name != 'pull_request' || contains(github.event.pull_request.labels.*.name, 'full-matrix') || contains(github.event.pull_request.labels.*.name, 'ci') || contains(github.event.pull_request.labels.*.name, 'release-matrix')) }}
        run: echo 'Local gauntlet evidence is the gate; request ci or full-matrix for CI.'

ci.yml.std-reference:
name: std reference gates
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v5
        with: {submodules: recursive}
      - uses: actions/setup-python@v5
        with: {python-version: '3.9'}
      - name: std extractor and drift controls
        run: python3 -m unittest discover -s tests -p '*_test.py' -v
      - name: generate std reference
        run: |
          mkdir -p dist
          cp -R site/. dist/
          python3 scripts/std-reference.py
          python3 scripts/render-std.py dist/std/reference.json dist/std
      - name: std public item completeness
        run: |
          python3 scripts/check-std.py
          python3 scripts/std-reference.py --check
          python3 scripts/render-std.py dist/std/reference.json dist/std --check
      - name: std two hops under production CSP and JavaScript off
        env:
          CHROMIUM: google-chrome
        run: node scripts/check-std-browser.mjs
ci.yml.build:
name: build the site
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v5
        with: {submodules: recursive}

      # The pins are the site's honesty guarantee: a page may not claim a
      # version of wolf that does not exist. Check them before anything
      # else, because everything else is generated from them.
      - name: submodule pins match their gitlinks
        run: |
          for m in wolf-book wolf-interp wolf-lang wolf-std; do
            want=$(git ls-tree HEAD "upstream/$m" | awk '{print $3}')
            have=$(git -C "upstream/$m" rev-parse HEAD)
            test "$want" = "$have" || { echo "::error::upstream/$m is $have, the pin says $want"; exit 1; }
            echo "$m ${have:0:7}"
          done

      # wolf-web#19. Every python script here runs twice — once on this
      # runner during the PR, once on the deploy host when trunk lands — and
      # for a while those were different interpreters with nothing saying so.
      # stamp-counts.py used a PEP 604 union in a nested signature; the runner
      # was 3.11+ where that is fine and the host is 3.9 where it raises at
      # call time, so a green PR run crashed the trunk deploy. The host's
      # version is written down in one place and installed here, so the PR run
      # IS the rehearsal: build.sh below runs seven of the eight scripts and the
      # link check runs the eighth, all under this interpreter.
      - name: the python the deploy host runs
        id: deploy-python
        run: |
          want=$(grep -v '^#' scripts/deploy-python.txt | tr -d '[:space:]')
          test -n "$want" || { echo "::error::scripts/deploy-python.txt names no version"; exit 1; }
          echo "version=$want" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          echo "the deploy host runs python3 $want; this job will too"
      - uses: actions/setup-python@v5
        with: {python-version: '${{ steps.deploy-python.outputs.version }}'}
      - name: and this job actually got it
        run: |
          have=$(python3 -c 'import sys; print("%d.%d" % sys.version_info[:2])')
          want='${{ steps.deploy-python.outputs.version }}'
          test "$have" = "$want" || { echo "::error::asked for python $want, this job has $have — the rehearsal would not be one"; exit 1; }
          python3 --version

      # The site states a DISTANCE now: how far the specification revision the
      # interpreter was built to sits behind the commit the compiler was tagged
      # at, in commits of the compiler's own history (scripts/stamp-counts.py,
      # `speccommits`). actions/checkout takes submodules at depth 1, which
      # cannot answer that. The deploy host clones with full history and needs
      # nothing here.
      - name: the pinned compiler checkout gets its history
        run: |
          if [ "$(git -C upstream/wolf-lang rev-parse --is-shallow-repository)" = true ]; then
            git -C upstream/wolf-lang fetch --quiet --unshallow --tags origin
          fi
          echo "upstream/wolf-lang carries $(git -C upstream/wolf-lang rev-list --count HEAD) commits"

      - uses: dtolnay/rust-toolchain@stable
      - name: the wasm target
        run: rustup target add wasm32-unknown-unknown

      # The book's PDF is typst-set. A pinned release binary, not
      # `cargo install`: the compile takes minutes and proves nothing.
      - name: typst (sets the book PDF)
        run: |
          curl -sSL https://github.com/typst/typst/releases/download/v0.15.1/typst-x86_64-unknown-linux-musl.tar.xz \
            | tar -xJ -C "$RUNNER_TEMP"
          echo "$RUNNER_TEMP/typst-x86_64-unknown-linux-musl" >> "$GITHUB_PATH"

      - name: shell scripts parse
        run: for f in scripts/*.sh; do bash -n "$f"; done

      # The editor's math is pure functions (site/play/editor-core.js) and
      # the CSP gate proves the doctrine: no new script sources, no inline
      # anything, no dependency creeping into the playground.
      - name: editor core and CSP gates
        run: node --test tests/*.test.mjs

      - name: std extractor controls
        run: python3 -m unittest discover -s tests -p '*_test.py'

      - name: build
        run: ./scripts/build.sh

      - name: the site has what it advertises
        run: |
          test -s dist/index.html
          # The prose tracks the pins: the stamped version is the pinned
          # CHANGELOG's, and no placeholder survives to the reader.
          wolfver=$(sed -n 's/^## \([0-9][0-9.]*\) .*/\1/p' upstream/wolf-lang/CHANGELOG.md | head -1)
          grep -q "This is version $wolfver" dist/index.html
          if grep -rq '__WOLF_VERSION__\|__LUPIN_VERSION__\|__PIN_' dist; then
            echo "::error::a version or revision placeholder reached dist/"; exit 1
          fi
          test -s dist/play/lupin.wasm
          test -s dist/version.json
          # wolf-web#26. The revisions this file publishes are seven hex
          # characters by decision, not whatever `git rev-parse --short` picks
          # from a repository's object count, so a post-deploy check can hold
          # them against a page's stamps by comparing bare strings. build.sh
          # refuses to write any other width; this is the served artifact
          # saying so where a reviewer of this workflow can see it.
          for p in $(python3 -c 'import json; v = json.load(open("dist/version.json")); print(" ".join(list(v["pins"].values()) + [v["spec-pin"]]))'); do
            echo "$p" | grep -Eq '^[0-9a-f]{7}$' || { echo "::error::version.json publishes '$p'; pins are seven hex characters"; exit 1; }
          done
          test -d dist/book
          test -s dist/book/wolf-book.pdf
          head -c 5 dist/book/wolf-book.pdf | grep -q '%PDF-'
          grep -q '/book/wolf-book.pdf' dist/reading/index.html
          python3 scripts/check-links.py dist
          python3 scripts/check-std.py
          python3 scripts/std-reference.py --check
          python3 scripts/render-std.py dist/std/reference.json dist/std --check

      # The menu is a promise. collect-samples.py can only read the corpus
      # header, which is the COMPILER's claim about a program; this feeds
      # every listed program to the wasm module the build just published and
      # holds what the PAGE says about it — an unnoted entry must run or trap,
      # and a noted one must not, so a note cannot outlive its refusal. Its
      # second half takes the whole of corpus/net/ through the same module,
      # because /play/ counts that directory and says the browser declines all
      # of it, and the count is stamped off the directory (wolf-web#17).
      - name: the playground's menu answers what the page claims
        run: node scripts/check-samples.mjs dist upstream/wolf-lang/corpus

      # The counted pin lag compares specification REVISIONS, so it is blind to
      # a clause the interpreter mirrors AHEAD of its pin — which it does on
      # purpose, with its own release notes saying so. At lupin 0.1.33 the gap
      # was zero, both pages said `the same commit`, and the tab ran a one-line
      # `if` the advertised compiler refused (wolf-web#35). Prose was all this
      # site had for it; this is the gate. Every witness that RUNS through the
      # module the build just published must name an anchor the pinned
      # release's own spec/anchors.json declares.
      - name: the tab runs nothing the advertised release does not carry
        run: node scripts/check-ahead.mjs dist upstream/wolf-lang

      # The gate above is green at this pin — its first witness closed at
      # v0.2.11 — and a gate nobody has watched fail is a claim. This suite
      # plants a witness that runs against a clause no release declares and
      # holds the refusal. It needs the built module, so it stands down in the
      # pre-build `node --test tests/*.test.mjs` above and is run again here.
      - name: the ahead gate reds on a planted case
        run: node --test tests/ahead-witnesses.test.mjs

      # Ruling #37 = B (wolf-web#55). lupin reads `cfg(target = …)` against
      # the target it was built for, and this module is built for wasm32,
      # which no `cfg` names; the bridge observes as x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu,
      # lupin's own bundle target. Only the wasm module can witness that, so
      # this suite stands down pre-build and must find the module here.
      - name: the tab reads cfg as x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu
        env:
          WOLF_WEB_REQUIRE_MODULE: "1"
        run: node --test tests/tab-target.test.mjs
ci.yml.deploy:
name: deploy to lupp.us
    needs: [build, std-reference]
    if: github.ref == 'refs/heads/trunk' && github.event_name == 'push'
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    concurrency: {group: deploy-lupp-us, cancel-in-progress: false}
    steps:
      - name: ssh to almanta and deploy trunk
        env:
          KEY: ${{ secrets.ALMANTA_DEPLOY_KEY }}
          HOST: ${{ secrets.ALMANTA_HOST }}
          USER: ${{ secrets.ALMANTA_USER }}
        run: |
          test -n "$KEY" || { echo "::error::ALMANTA_DEPLOY_KEY is not set"; exit 1; }
          # scripts/ci-deploy.sh on the host prints its own python3 beside the
          # version the build job rehearsed on, and refuses when they differ
          # (wolf-web#19). Both numbers land in this log.
          install -m 700 -d ~/.ssh
          printf '%s\n' "$KEY" > ~/.ssh/deploy && chmod 600 ~/.ssh/deploy
          ssh-keyscan -H "$HOST" >> ~/.ssh/known_hosts 2>/dev/null
          # The key is restricted to scripts/ci-deploy.sh on the server, so
          # this command string is ignored; it is here for the log.
          ssh -i ~/.ssh/deploy -o BatchMode=yes "$USER@$HOST" deploy
